author: reek
body: The boot ring gave proc 0 its scope from the compiler. This is the other door into a process table: a signed binary, verified against a trust lattice and a policy, whose approved grant is written into a slot the new process will run under. Until now only half the grant made that journey. The verifier decoded the scope -- it always could, the format carries it -- and CapGrant then folded the capability list into a bare bitmask and dropped it. A binary whose manifest said "filesystem read, under /config/" was loaded with filesystem read over the whole volume: the authority arrived and the limit on it did not, which is the worse half to lose.

author: reek
body: Two binaries are built here, identical but for the scope literal, and that comparison is the test. The scoped one must arrive scoped. The unscoped one must arrive unscoped -- and that half matters, because a loader that wrote "/config/" into every slot regardless would pass a test that only ever checked the scoped case.
